A. Purpose: To provide guideline instruction for surgical care services with the aim that

  • Need and expectations of the patients are established.
  • Patient satisfaction is enhanced on a continuous basis.

B. Scope: It covers all patients undergoing any form of surgical treatment in the hospital.

C. Responsibility Person: consultant of Surgery

D. Departmental Hierarchy:

Consultant - Surgery

Staff Nurse

Housekeeping Staff.

E. Policy:

1. Qualification of staff:

  • Surgical care is provided by post graduate qualified and experienced surgeons.
  • Anesthesia is provided by post graduate qualified and experienced anesthesia.
  • Nursing care in the OT is provided by qualified and registered nursing staff.

2. Patient Assessment:

a. Surgical OPD

  • Patient visit the surgical OPD either by themselves anticipating their problem or are guided by the registration counter clerk.
  • Patients are also referred by other clinicians as per the care needed by the patient.
  • Initial Assessment includes patient’s past medical history, general examination and routine investigations to confirm patient’s need for surgical intervention.
  • In case the patient needs cardiac assessment prior to surgery, the patient is referred to the cardiologist for evaluation.
  • After confirming the patient’s need for surgical intervention the plan of care is drawn by the surgeon of the patient.
  • Patients and their relatives are informed about the need for surgery, expected outcome, risk involved, prognosis of the patient etc. by the concerned surgeon.
  • The date and time of surgery is scheduled and the patient is informed to get admitted a day before the scheduled date of surgery for undergoing all needed preparation including the required investigations.

b. Emergency Department:

  • Patients directly visit the emergency department of the hospital.
  • The emergency medical officer on duty immediately attends the patients and undertakes the initial assessment to determine the care needed by the patient.
  • In case the patient needs surgical intervention, the surgeon on call is immediately informed by the on duty EMO.
  • The patient is attended by the surgeon who evaluates the patient’s condition and the need for surgical intervention.
  • If the patient’s need for surgical intervention is not immediate in nature the patient is admitted for further evaluation prior to the surgery.
  • In case the patient’s condition is severe and requires immediate surgical intervention, the surgeon informs the patient relatives about the need for immediate surgical intervention for saving the life of the patient, outcome expected, risk involved etc.

3. Preoperative Assessment:

Once the patients need for surgical intervention is established the patients has to undergo a preoperative checkup by the concerned surgeon which include the following:

  • Patients Vitals
  • Blood Pressure, Cardiac Rhythm etc.
  • Examination of the chest.
  • Investigation such as X-Ray chest, ECG etc.

The patient’s preoperative checkup findings is documented in the specified format in the patient’s case sheet.

The preoperative checkup for patients requiring immediate surgical intervention is done immediately after the surgeon’s decision for emergency surgical intervention.

After the preoperative check up by the surgeon, the patient is referred to the anesthetist for pre-anesthesia checkup.

4. Pre anesthesia Checkup:

The consultant anesthetist undertakes the pre-anesthesia checkup the patient which includes the following:

  • Medical History such as HT/Dm/ Chest Pain etc.
  • Surgical and Anesthetics history if any
  • General Examination such as Pulse, BP, RR etc.
  • Systemic Examinations etc.

All pre-anesthesia check-up findings are documented in the specified format attached with the patients IPD File (BHT).

The pre Anesthesia checkup for patients requiring immediate surgical intervention is done immediately after the surgeon’s decision for emergency surgical intervention.

5. Preoperative order to the nursing staff:

A. Ward Nursing Staff:-

The preoperative order to the nursing staff of the concerned ward where the patient is admitted includes the following:

  • Drug orders for example morbidity medications like antihypertensive drugs etc.
  • Patient preparation instructions including marking of the surgical site etc.
  • Time and date of surgery.
  • Specific documents such as X-Ray plates etc., if any to be forwarded along with the patient to the OT.

B. OT Nursing Staff:-

  • List of patient to be operated should be prepared a day prior to the scheduled day of surgery.
  • List should include a patient wise distribution of scheduled surgeries; type of anesthesia to be administered. The information thus prepared is to be informed to the consultant surgeons and anesthetist.

6. Informed Consent for Surgery:

Consent for the patients and or relatives for the surgery is obtained by the operating surgeon in the specified format after explaining the following details:

  • Nature of Surgery.
  • Reason for the procedure.
  • Expected Outcome.
  • Risk Involved.
  • Expected duration of recovery etc.

The consent is obtained from the patient and or the surrogate as per the hospital’s policy a day prior to the scheduled date for the surgery.

7. Prevention of Wrong Procedure/Side/Site and Wrong Patient:

The prevention of wrong site/ side/procedure and patient begins with the preoperative evaluation of the patient.

This involves the following activities such as marking of the surgical side, verification of patient prior to the shifting of the patient from the ward to the OT, at the time of patient’s entrance to the OT suite and prior to the initiation of the procedure inside the theatres, etc.

The policy for prevention of wrong procedure/side/site and patient could be referred for the hospital’s detailed policy.

8. Transfer of Patient to Operation Theatre:

  • Prior to the transfer of the patient the ward nurse informs the OT nurse about the patient details and confirms the scheduled time for surgery forty five minutes prior to the scheduled time of surgery.
  • The ward nurse prior to the transfer of the patient ensures that the nurse’s preoperative checklist is dully filled and all the patient details as required by the surgeons are arranged in the proper order.
  • The patient is transferred to the OT as per the hospital’s intramural transfer policy.

9. Receiving of patient and immediate preoperative assessment:

  • The patient is received in the preoperative patient holding area of the theatre.
  • The OT nurse evaluates the patient’s details and checks the preoperative nursing checklist filled by the ward nurse to ensure the patients preparedness and confirms the patient’s identity as per the IPD File.
  • The patient is transferred to the operating rooms where the concerned surgeon and anesthetist undertake immediate preoperative evaluation.

10. Post-Surgery Process:

    • Post Operation the patient is shifted to the post-operative recovery area of the OT suite.
    • In the recovery area patient is kept under the supervision of the specialist anesthetist, consultant surgeon nursing care in the post-operative area is provided by Operation Theatre nurses.
    • Prior to discharge from the post-operative recovery area a brief operative note is documented by the concerned surgeon in the patient’s IPD File.
    • The consultant surgeon documents the post-operative condition of the patient, post-operative treatment plan etc. The surgeon concerned will not leave the hospital until and unless he/she is assured about the stable condition of the patient
    • Post-operative treatment plan includes informs regarding the need for keeping the patient under intensive care, post-operative medications, examinations required if any etc.

11. Quality Assurance Programme for Surgical Services:

Surgical service is a very specialized specialty of medicine and there is a need of quality in everything. Quality in surgical services is achieved through:

  • Surgery of any type is done only by appropriately qualified (as per MCI guidelines) and experienced surgeons.
  • Any form of Anesthesia is administered by Qualified Anesthetist (MCI guidelines).
  • Nursing care is provided by qualified, trained and experienced nursing staff registered with Nursing Council.
  • Documentation of patient’s surgical plan ( Ref Patients Case File)
  • Documentation of patient’s preoperative condition
  • Pre-operative Surgeons Assessment
  • Pre-operative Anesthetist Assessment
  • Pre-operative Nursing Checklist.
  • Immediate pre-operative assessment of the patient by the consultant surgeon and the anesthetist.
  • Transfer of patient to the OT is done by designated staff
  • Time based intra operative monitoring of the patient by the anesthetist
  • Post-surgery monitoring of the patient in the post-operative recovery area
  • Documentation of the surgical procedures performed, outcome, post-operative condition of the patient and post-operative treatment plan etc. by the consultant surgeon.
  • Appropriate zoning of the operating theatre suite and strict adherence to infection control activities in the operating theatre complex.
  • Well established method for reporting any surgical site infection, its analysis by a multidisciplinary committee for formulation of adequate control and prevention plan.

Policy & Procedure for Non-Surgical Procedures

A. PURPOSE

To establish standardized guidelines for the safe, effective, and consistent performance of non-surgical procedures in the hospital, ensuring:

  • Patient safety and comfort
  • Standardization of clinical practices
  • Compliance with NABH and regulatory requirements

B. SCOPE

This policy applies to:

  • All departments performing non-surgical procedures (OPD, IPD, Emergency, ICU)
  • All healthcare professionals involved (Doctors, Nurses, Technicians)

Examples of Non-Surgical Procedures:

  • Injections (IV/IM/SC)
  • Catheterization
  • Wound dressing
  • Suturing (minor)
  • Nebulization

C. POLICY STATEMENT

The hospital ensures that:

  • All non-surgical procedures are performed by trained and authorized personnel
  • Proper consent is obtained before procedures
  • Standard precautions and aseptic techniques are followed
  • Documentation is complete and accurate
  • Patient rights, dignity, and privacy are maintained

D. DEFINITIONS

  • Non-Surgical Procedure: Any diagnostic or therapeutic intervention that does not involve major surgical incision or operation
  • Informed Consent: Voluntary agreement by the patient after understanding the procedure

E. RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Medical Officer / Consultant

  • Assess patient and prescribe procedure
  • Obtain informed consent
  • Supervise and manage complications

2. Nursing Staff

  • Prepare patient and equipment
  • Assist or perform procedure
  • Monitor patient before, during, and after procedure
  • Maintain documentation

3. Technicians

  • Operate equipment safely
  • Ensure calibration and maintenance

4. Infection Control Team

  • Ensure adherence to infection prevention protocols

F. PROCEDURE

1. Pre-Procedure Phase

  • Verify patient identity (Name, UHID, DOB)
  • Confirm procedure order
  • Obtain informed consent
  • Explain procedure to patient/guardian
  • Check allergies and medical history
  • Ensure availability of required equipment and emergency drugs
  • Perform hand hygiene
  • Use appropriate PPE

2. During Procedure

  • Maintain aseptic technique
  • Ensure patient comfort and privacy
  • Follow standard clinical protocols
  • Monitor vital signs
  • Use sterile/clean equipment as applicable
  • Communicate with patient throughout procedure

3. Post-Procedure Care

  • Monitor patient for complications
  • Provide post-procedure instructions
  • Dispose biomedical waste as per policy
  • Clean and disinfect equipment
  • Document procedure details

G. SAFETY & INFECTION CONTROL

  • Follow Standard Precautions at all times
  • Use PPE (gloves, masks, gowns as required)
  • Safe injection practices
  • Proper biomedical waste segregation
  • Hand hygiene compliance

H. CONSENT GUIDELINES

  • Written consent for:
    • Invasive procedures
    • Endoscopy, dialysis, catheterization
  • Verbal consent for minor procedures
  • Consent must include:
    • Procedure details
    • Risks and benefits
    • Alternatives
